Read an MDArray from a multidimensional raster, with dimension information

Source: R/gdal_mdim.R
mdim_read.Rd

mdim_read() reads all or part of an array in a GDAL Multidimensional Raster dataset, and returns a vector with an attribute "gis" describing the dimensions and coordinates of the values read. It is the multidimensional counterpart of read_ds(), and uses GDALMDArray$read(). Requires GDAL >= 3.2. This function is experimental. Its interface may change in future releases.

Usage

mdim_read(
  x,
  array_name,
  start = NULL,
  count = NULL,
  step = NULL,
  as_array = FALSE,
  as_raw = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

Either an object of class GDALMultiDimRaster, or a character string giving the data source name of a multidimensional raster (which is opened read-only and closed on return).

array_name

Character string giving the full path of the array in the dataset, e.g., "/temperature" or "/group/temperature".

start

Optional numeric vector of 0-based start indexes, one value per dimension of the array, in the array's own dimension order. Defaults to 0 for each dimension.

count

Optional numeric vector of the number of values to read along each dimension. Defaults to the rest of each dimension after start (taking step into account).

step

Optional numeric vector of the step between indexes along each dimension. Defaults to 1 for each dimension.

as_array

Logical value. If TRUE, also set the dim attribute of the returned vector to gis$dim, so that it can be used as an R array indexed as [x, y, ...]. Defaults to FALSE.

as_raw

Logical value. If TRUE and the array data type is Byte, return values as R raw. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

A vector of values, with attribute "gis" (and dim if as_array = TRUE). See Details.

Details

Values are returned as stored, in the same order as returned by GDALMDArray$read(): the last dimension of the array varies fastest. Scale and offset are not applied (the unscaled value is value * gis$scale + gis$offset), and the nodata value is returned as NA.

The "gis" attribute is a list with elements:

  • type: "multidim"

  • dim: the number of values read along each dimension, fastest varying first, i.e., the reverse of the array's dimension order (the same convention as c(xsize, ysize, nbands) in the "gis" attribute from read_ds())

  • dim_names: the dimension names, in the same order as dim

  • coords: a named list, in the same order as dim, with the coordinate values of each dimension for the values read, or NULL for a dimension without an indexing variable

  • bbox: c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) from the coordinates of the horizontal dimensions (cell edges, assuming regular spacing), or NA values if they cannot be determined

  • srs: the spatial reference system as WKT, or ""

  • datatype: the data type name (e.g., "Int16")

  • nodata, scale, offset: numeric values, NA if not set

  • unit: the unit of the array values, or ""

  • dim_units: the units of the dimension coordinates, in the same order as dim (e.g., "degrees_east", "hours since 1900-01-01"), "" if not set

  • calendar: the calendar attribute of the time coordinate if present (e.g., "standard", "noleap"), otherwise NA.

Units and calendars are returned as stored, as character strings.

The horizontal dimensions are those with type HORIZONTAL_X and HORIZONTAL_Y, or otherwise the last and second last dimensions of the array.

See also

GDALMultiDimRaster, GDALMDArray, read_ds()

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata/mdim_small.nc", package="gdalraster")

v <- mdim_read(f, "/t2m")
str(attr(v, "gis"))
#> List of 13
#>  $ type     : chr "multidim"
#>  $ dim      : num [1:3] 6 5 4
#>  $ dim_names: chr [1:3] "lon" "lat" "time"
#>  $ coords   :List of 3
#>   ..$ lon : num [1:6] 145 145 146 146 146 ...
#>   ..$ lat : num [1:5] -41 -41.2 -41.5 -41.8 -42
#>   ..$ time: num [1:4] 0 6 12 18
#>  $ bbox     : num [1:4] 144.9 -42.1 146.4 -40.9
#>  $ srs      : chr ""
#>  $ datatype : chr "Int16"
#>  $ nodata   : num -32767
#>  $ scale    : num 0.01
#>  $ offset   : num 0
#>  $ unit     : chr "degC"
#>  $ dim_units: chr [1:3] "degrees_east" "degrees_north" "hours since 2000-01-01 00:00:00"
#>  $ calendar : chr "standard"

# the first time step as an R matrix [lon, lat], in degC
ds <- new(GDALMultiDimRaster, f)
v <- mdim_read(ds, "/t2m", start = c(0, 0, 0), count = c(1, 5, 6),
               as_array = TRUE)
gis <- attr(v, "gis")
gis$dim
#> [1] 6 5 1
gis$coords
#> $lon
#> [1] 145.00 145.25 145.50 145.75 146.00 146.25
#> 
#> $lat
#> [1] -41.00 -41.25 -41.50 -41.75 -42.00
#> 
#> $time
#> [1] 0
#> 
v[, , 1] * gis$scale + gis$offset
#>       [,1]  [,2]  [,3]  [,4]  [,5]
#> [1,] 12.95 13.55 14.15 14.75 15.35
#> [2,] 13.05 13.65 14.25 14.85 15.45
#> [3,]    NA 13.75 14.35 14.95 15.55
#> [4,] 13.25 13.85 14.45 15.05 15.65
#> [5,] 13.35 13.95 14.55 15.15 15.75
#> [6,] 13.45 14.05 14.65 15.25 15.85
ds$close()
